items.headline: Albemarle quarterly profit beats expectations on rising lithium prices
items.snippet: Albemarle, the world's largest producer of lithium for batteries, posted a better-than-expected quarterly profit as prices for the ultra-light metal jumped. Albemarle said the average price it received for its lithium rose 61% during the quarter and its sales volumes increased 11

items.headline: Albemarle Swings To Q2 Profit
items.snippet: Albemarle Corp reported second-quarter net income of $438.3 million ($3.52/share) vs a loss a year ago. Net sales increased 31.1% to $1.74 billion. Energy Storage net sales climbed 78% to $1.28 billion, primarily due to higher lithium prices.

items.headline: Albemarle price target lowered to $161 from $189 at Morgan Stanley
items.snippet: Morgan Stanley analyst Vincent Andrews lowered the firm's price target on Albemarle to $161 from $189 and keeps an Equal Weight rating, saying lithium prices have come off this cycle's peak, reducing the multiple assigned to Albemarle's lithium EBITDA.

items.headline: Albemarle price target lowered to $225 from $245 at Truist
items.snippet: Truist analyst Peter Osterland lowered the firm's price target on Albemarle to $225 from $245 and keeps a Buy rating on the shares, citing resilient lithium demand and constrained supply dynamics against an overly discounted valuation.
